## Situation
Invoice 1042 for $2,400 was due Oct 30 and is now 16 days late.
Dana at Example Design Studio is a good client and this is the first time they are late, so start friendly.

## Email 1, send today
Subject: Invoice 1042: a quick reminder

Hi Dana,

I hope all is well. A quick note that invoice 1042 for $2,400 was due Oct 30 and still shows as open on my side. It may simply have slipped through.

You can pay here: https://pay.example.com/1042

If it is already on its way, please ignore this note. Thank you!

Alex
Bright Studio

## Email 2, send in 7 days if unpaid
Subject: Invoice 1042 for $2,400 is still open

Hi Dana,

I am following up on invoice 1042 for $2,400, which was due Oct 30 and is still unpaid.

Could you tell me the date you will send payment? You can pay here: https://pay.example.com/1042

If something is holding it up, tell me and we will sort it out together.

Alex
Bright Studio

## Email 3, send in 14 days if unpaid
Subject: Final reminder: invoice 1042 for $2,400

Hi Dana,

This is my final reminder about invoice 1042 for $2,400, which was due Oct 30. I have written twice and have not had a payment or a date.

Please pay it this week, or reply today with the date you will pay. You can pay here: https://pay.example.com/1042

If there is a problem with the invoice or the work, tell me now so we can fix it.

Alex
Bright Studio

## Phone script
"Hi Dana, it's Alex from Bright Studio. I'm calling about invoice 1042 for $2,400. It was due Oct 30 and I have not seen it come in. Is anything holding it up on your side?"
Listen first. Then ask: "What date can I note down for the payment?"

## Do not say
- "You always pay late." It is not true: this is their first time.
- "I really need this money." It makes a business matter personal.
- "This is your last chance." It sounds like a threat, and you have not decided on any next step.

landing-page-teardown.sample_output:
## Scorecard

| Criterion | Score | Evidence | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Clear in 5 seconds | 1 | "delivers best-in-class visual solutions for modern brands" | The first screen never says product photos or online shops. A shop owner coming from an ad has to scroll to "What we do" to find out. |
| 2. Specific outcome | 3 | "we send back edited images that are ready to upload to your shop" | Concrete and useful, but it sits in the third block, not at the top. |
| 3. Proof | 0 | missing | No review, customer name, number or sample photo is on the page. "online shops of every size" is a claim, not proof. |
| 4. Objections | 2 | "Every pack includes one round of changes." | One worry is answered. Nothing on how long it takes, on posting products, or on what happens if the photos miss. |
| 5. Call to action | 1 | "Send us a message, follow us on Instagram, or sign up for our newsletter." | Three actions compete and none of them is "Book a call". The ask shows once, at the very bottom. |
| 6. Friction | 2 | "Bright Studio started in a spare room with one camera and a big dream." | The story comes before the offer, so the visitor reads about you before learning what they get. There is no booking step on the page. |
| 7. Voice | 2 | "We are passionate about quality." | Filler at the top ("passionate", "best-in-class", "solutions"). The "What we do" block does sound like a person. |
| 8. Offer and price | 4 | "Starter pack: 10 edited photos, $600." | Two packs with clear prices and what is in each. They sit halfway down the page. |

Total: 15/40

Biggest problem: the first screen does not say this is product photography for online shops, and the page never asks the visitor to book a call.

## New hero

**Headline:** Product photos for your online shop, from $600
**Subhead:** Post us your products. We shoot them on clean backgrounds and in styled scenes, and email back edited photos ready to upload.
**Button:** Book a call

## Three other headlines

- Outcome: Edited product photos, ready to upload to your shop
- Pain: Your products deserve better than a quick phone photo
- Proof: [add: a real customer result, such as a shop's name and what changed for them]

## Top 5 fixes

| Fix | Where on the page | Impact | Effort (minutes) | Exactly what to write or cut |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Replace the hero | Top of the page | High | 10 | Cut "We are passionate about quality." and the "best-in-class visual solutions" sentence. Put in the new headline, subhead and button. |
| 2. Ask for one action | "Get in touch" and under the hero | High | 15 | Cut "follow us on Instagram, or sign up for our newsletter". Make "Book a call" the only button: under the hero, after the packs and at the end. [confirm: the link to your booking calendar] |
| 3. Add proof | Under the hero | High | 30 | [add: customer reviews with each shop's name] and [add: before and after photos from a real job]. |
| 4. Move the packs up | "Our packs" | Medium | 5 | Put "Our packs" right after "What we do". Move "Our story" to the end of the page. |
| 5. Answer the worries | After "Our packs" | Medium | 20 | Keep "Every pack includes one round of changes." Add one line each on timing [confirm: how long a pack takes], on posting [confirm: who pays for postage and how products come back] and on a miss [confirm: what you do if the buyer is not happy]. |

## One section rewritten: "Why choose us"

Before:
> We care about details. We are easy to work with. We love what we do, and it shows in our work.

After:
> **Why shop owners pick us**
> - Clean backgrounds and styled scenes.
> - Photos come back edited and ready to upload.
> - One round of changes is included in every pack.
> - [add: one customer review with the shop's name]

## What to keep

- The prices are on the page and easy to read: "Starter pack: 10 edited photos, $600."
- "How it works" is three short, plain steps.

faq.q: Does it look at my design, images or page speed?
faq.a: No. It reads only the words you paste. It cannot see layout, images or how fast the page loads.

faq.q: Will it make up reviews or numbers for my page?
faq.a: No. It uses only what is on your page and in your offer. Where proof is missing it writes [add: ...] so you know what to add yourself.

faq.q: Can I run it again after I change the page?
faq.a: Yes. Each run scores the text you paste that time, so you can compare the two totals.

# Proposal: workshop booking page and product photos
For Sam, from Alex at Bright Studio

## What you asked for
You run a small online candle shop and you are adding candle-making workshops. You need a booking page so people can reserve a workshop seat, and 10 product photos for the shop, all before March 1. You also asked about a short video for Instagram.

## What we will deliver
- One booking page where people can reserve a workshop seat.
- 10 product photos for your shop.

## What is not included
- Taking payment for a seat on the booking page. [confirm: reserve only, or pay when reserving]
- Changes to the rest of your shop's site.
- The short video for Instagram. It is not priced in this proposal. [confirm: whether you offer video, and the price]
- Ongoing updates after launch. See the optional Monthly care plan below.

## Timeline
3 weeks from kickoff. To deliver before March 1 we need to start in time. [confirm: the kickoff date]

## Investment
| Item | Quantity | Unit price | Line total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Booking page build | 1 | $1,800 | $1,800 |
| Product photo | 10 | $60 each | $600 |

1,800 + (10 x 60) = 2,400
Total: $2,400

Optional, per month: Monthly care plan, $150. Not in the total.

## Payment
50% upfront, 50% on delivery.
- Upfront: $1,200
- On delivery: $1,200

## Next step
Reply with a yes and a start date. I will then send the invoice for the first $1,200 and we begin.

---

## Cover email

Subject: Proposal: your workshop booking page and 10 product photos

Hi Sam,

Thank you for the brief. The proposal is attached. It covers a booking page so people can reserve a workshop seat, and 10 product photos for your shop, planned for delivery before March 1. The total is $2,400.

Could we have a short call this week to settle the open questions and agree a start date?

Alex
Bright Studio

---

## Before you send

To be priced by you:
- [ ] A short video for Instagram. It has no price on your list and is not in the total. Price it, or tell the client you do not offer it.

Questions for the client:
- [ ] Should people pay when they reserve a seat, or only reserve?
- [ ] How many workshops are planned, and how many seats in each?
- [ ] Where should the booking page live: on your current shop site or somewhere new?
- [ ] For the Instagram video: how long should it be and what should it show?
- [ ] When can we start, so that we deliver before March 1?

faq.q: Will it invent a price?
faq.a: No. It uses only the prices on your list, exactly as you wrote them. Anything the client needs that has no price goes under "To be priced by you" and stays out of the total.

faq.q: Can I trust the totals?
faq.a: The sum is written out line by line so you can check it in seconds. Check it before you send.

faq.q: Does it send the proposal to my client?
faq.a: No. Nothing is sent. You copy the proposal and the cover email and send them yourself.

version.notes: First version. Sets the scope, builds a pricing table from your own prices with the sum shown, then writes the proposal, a cover email and a checklist of what to settle before you send. Nothing is sent.

## Your carousel copy

### 1. Slides

1. **Your photos are costing you sales**

2. **Mistake 1: Dark, uneven light**
   Shoppers can't judge what they can't see. Shoot next to a window in daylight and turn the lamps off.

3. **Mistake 2: A busy background**
   Clutter pulls the eye away from the product. Use one plain surface and one plain wall.

4. **Mistake 3: Only one angle**
   Online, nobody can pick it up. Show the front, the back, the side and one close detail.

5. **Mistake 4: No sense of size**
   People guess the size and guess wrong. Add one photo with a hand or an everyday object.

6. **Mistake 5: Every photo looks different**
   Mixed crops and colors make a shop look careless. Pick one crop and one background, and keep them.

7. **Save this for later**
   Check your next five photos against this list.

### 2. Caption

Good products lose sales to bad photos. Here are five mistakes small shops make, and the simple fix for each: light, background, angles, size and consistency. None of them needs a new camera. Pick the one you see most in your own shop and fix it this week. Save this for later.

### 3. Hashtags

#productphotography #productphotos #onlineshopowner #smallshoptips #ecommercephotos

### 4. Alt text

A seven-slide carousel that lists five product photo mistakes small online shops make, with a short fix for each.

## Day 1
Format: Reel
Hook: Half a day on the water, start to finish.
Show: Phone clips from last weekend's trips, cut in the order of the day: leaving the dock, open water, the ride back.
Caption: Half a day is enough. You leave the dock, the town gets small, and the afternoon is yours. This is last weekend, with nothing added.
Call to action: Save this for your trip.

## Day 2
Format: Story
Hook: Meet the captain who takes you out.
Show: A few story frames of the captain on the boat: a hello to camera, the checks before a trip, then a question box.
Caption: This is [confirm: the captain's name]. The person at the helm matters, so ask anything you would want to know before a day on the water.
Call to action: Put your question in the box.

## Day 3
Format: Carousel
Hook: What a private half day looks like, part by part.
Show: Stills taken from last weekend's clips, in order: the hook over the boat, leaving the dock, open water, the stop at [confirm: where the trip stops], the ride back.
Caption: A private half-day trip, part by part. Your group, the boat, and an unhurried stretch of the day. What is included: [confirm: what the trip includes].
Call to action: Send this to the person you would bring.

## Day 4
Format: Reel
Hook: Your group, your boat, nobody else on board.
Show: The guest who agreed to be filmed, on board with their group. This clip is not filmed yet: film it before Day 4, or use last weekend's clips of a group on deck.
Caption: Private means the boat is yours for the half day. Bring the people you came here with and keep the afternoon to yourselves.
Call to action: Message us to ask about a weekend date for your group.

## Day 5
Format: Story
Hook: Tonight's sunset trip, as it happens.
Show: Story frames filmed during Friday's sunset trip: boarding, the light changing, the captain at the helm.
Caption: We are out for sunset this evening. Follow along as the light changes.
Call to action: Reply to this story with a question.

## Day 6
Format: Carousel
Hook: Questions small groups ask before a boat day.
Show: A question on each slide with a short answer under it: is it private (yes), how many people ([confirm: the largest group you take]), what to bring ([confirm: what guests should bring]). Use stills from last weekend's clips behind the text.
Caption: The questions small groups ask before a boat day, answered plainly. If yours is not here, ask us and we will add it.
Call to action: Send us the question we missed.

## Day 7
Format: Reel
Hook: Next weekend could look like this.
Show: The best few seconds from Friday's sunset trip, then the guest clip, ending on the boat at the dock.
Caption: Your group, the boat, half a day. If you are in town on a weekend, this is a calm way to spend part of it.

review-replies.name: Google Review Replies
review-replies.summary: A public reply for each review you paste, in your voice, plus a short list of the reviews you should follow up on yourself. Nothing is posted.
review-replies.description:
Paste your latest reviews. It reads each one, notes how the person feels and the specific thing they mention, then writes one public reply per review in your voice. It ends with the short list of reviews that need a personal follow-up, and what to do first. Nothing is posted for you: you copy each reply where you want it.

You provide: your business name and what you offer, the reviews (one per line), and (optional) your voice and how an unhappy guest can reach you.

You get: a numbered reply for every review, in the order you pasted them, then the follow-up list.

Limits: up to 20 reviews a run. It never offers a refund, a discount or anything free, never promises a fix, never argues, and does not confirm a complaint you have not checked yet. It uses only what the reviews and you say. It does not read or post to any review site: you paste and you copy.
